title: Apple and grape bircher with hazelnuts

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food: oats, fresh fruit, raisins, nuts, seeds and cinnamon, with no jars, packet mixes or plant milks.

supermarket.reason: Oats, grapes, apples, oranges, hazelnuts and pumpkin seeds are all everyday items at Tesco.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a bowl, a grater and a knife and board, and the technique is simple stirring and grating.

works.reason: The juice of two oranges plus 300ml water to 200g oats is a sensible soaking ratio, and with apple, grapes and nuts it gives four good bowls.

honest_times.reason: About 15 minutes of active work covers juicing, grating, halving 300g of grapes and chopping nuts, and the 480 minutes is an unattended overnight soak as noted.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing extra appears beyond a splash of water.

seasonal_feel.reason: Grapes are a main part of the dish, both folded through and scattered on top, alongside November apples, and a bircher is a reasonable autumn breakfast.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, friendly British English, with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Oats, fresh fruit, nuts and seeds make a filling, wholesome breakfast that a family would happily eat.
